title: Delhi road-crash victims (killed and injured) by category of road user, 2004 to 2018, as printed in Table 3.1
scope: Delhi as a whole, persons (not crashes). Fatalities and injuries by the victim's category of road user, from the Delhi Traffic Police annual reports. Not split by district. Counts, not rates.
categories: Pedestrians; cyclists; car occupants; scooter and motorcycle riders; bus passengers; slow-moving vehicles (hand cart, electric rickshaw and cycle rickshaw pullers and passengers, as printed); drivers of animal-driven vehicles; other drivers; total.

sources.describes: Table 3.1 for 2001 to 2015 (printed page 15); used only to check the 2004 to 2014 rows of the 2018 table by eye
sources.kind: Delhi Traffic Police, Road Accidents in Delhi 2015, chapter 3 (Victims of Road Accidents)

sources.describes: Table 3.1 for 2004 to 2018 (printed page 22); the source of every row
sources.kind: Delhi Traffic Police, Road Accidents in Delhi 2018, chapter 3 (Victims of road accidents)

checks: Every year: the eight categories add up to the printed total for killed and for injured.
Every year from 2011: the killed total equals the citywide trend in data/road_safety_trends.json.
caveats: These categories are the 2004 to 2018 reports' own. The 2019 to 2024 mode-of-travel figures on the site come from a later report series with its own category labels (for example "two-wheeler riders"); the two series are close in meaning but a join across 2018 and 2019 should be read with caution.
The totals are persons killed or injured and are not the same count as fatal crashes.
A category share is the share of persons killed that year in that category.
2001 to 2003 are printed in the 2015 report but their categories do not add up to the printed totals, so they are not included.
Single-agent transcription from page images; not independently reviewed. No explicit open licence verified; cite the Traffic Police report.
